quest85.title: The Archivist's Cover
quest85.rationale:
The Archivist's Cover

Why it's important:
Book cover design combines illustration, typography, composition, and visual storytelling. It teaches students to communicate a book's essence visually while working within design constraints. No bookbinding knowledge required.

Skills developed:

  • Visual communication and storytelling
  • Typography and layout
  • Illustration and imagery
  • Composition and hierarchy
  • Design thinking and audience awareness
quest85.description: The Archivist's library holds thousands of books, but many covers have faded beyond recognition. You must select a book and redesign its cover, capturing its essence through original illustration and typography.
requirements: Select a book (fiction or non-fiction)
Create a new cover design (front cover minimum, full wrap optional)
Include original illustration or imagery
Include title and author typography
Show clear connection to the book's content or themes
Finish with a clean, professional presentation

levels.4: Professional-level illustration and typography; polished finish.
levels.3: Good technique; clean work with minor issues.
levels.2: Basic technique; some rough areas.
levels.1: Poor technique; unfinished or messy.

levels.4: Exceptional layout; strong hierarchy; visually compelling.
levels.3: Good composition; clear hierarchy.
levels.2: Basic composition; layout is unclear.
levels.1: Poor composition; disorganized.

levels.4: Deep connection to book's themes; cover communicates essence effectively.
levels.3: Clear connection to book; cover is appropriate.
levels.2: Weak connection; cover is generic.
levels.1: No connection; cover unrelated to book.

quest89.title: The Architect's Trial
quest89.rationale:
The Architect's Trial

Why it's important:
Perspective is the backbone of spatial drawing. This summative challenges students to demonstrate mastery of multiple perspective systems in one cohesive work.

Skills developed:

  • 1-point, 2-point, 3-point, 4-point, and 5-point perspective
  • Foreshortening
  • Spatial coherence across multiple systems
  • Compositional planning
  • Line precision and consistency
quest89.description: The Grand Architect challenges you to create a single drawing that demonstrates mastery of at least 3 different perspective systems. The composition should be cohesive, not a collection of separate studies.
requirements: Create a single cohesive drawing
Demonstrate at least 3 perspective systems
Maintain spatial consistency
Show accurate vanishing points and horizon lines
Finish with clean, confident linework

levels.4: Multiple strong compositional approaches explored; clear planning evident.
levels.3: Good planning with some exploration of approaches.
levels.2: Limited planning; single approach taken.
levels.1: No evidence of planning.

levels.4: All perspective systems are accurate and consistent; vanishing points are precise.
levels.3: Most perspective systems are accurate with minor errors.
levels.2: Some perspective errors; spatial consistency is inconsistent.
levels.1: Perspective is incorrect or unclear.

levels.4: Composition is cohesive and balanced; spatial relationships are clear across all systems.
levels.3: Composition is mostly cohesive; spatial relationships are readable.
levels.2: Composition is uneven; spatial relationships are confusing.
levels.1: Composition is disorganized; spatial relationships are unclear.

levels.4: Thorough documentation of perspective studies and composition plan.
levels.3: Good documentation with minor gaps.
levels.2: Basic documentation; missing key stages.
levels.1: No documentation or process evidence.

quest90.title: The Sunweaver's Alchemy
quest90.rationale:
The Sunweaver's Alchemy

Why it's important:
Cyanotype is a 19th-century photographic printing process that uses sunlight and iron salts to create blue-toned images. It teaches composition, negative/positive space, and the interaction of light with materials—all without a darkroom or expensive equipment.

Skills developed:

  • Composition with found objects and stencils
  • Understanding of light-sensitive processes
  • Negative and positive space
  • Patience and timing
  • Layering and exposure control
quest90.description: The Sunweaver's Guild guards the secret of capturing light on paper. You are tasked with creating cyanotype prints—arranging objects, stencils, or drawings on treated paper and exposing them to sunlight to reveal blue-toned images.
requirements: Create at least 2 cyanotype prints
Use found objects, stencils, or drawn transparencies
Show intentional composition
Demonstrate control of exposure time
Finish with proper washing and drying

levels.4: Excellent exposure control; crisp edges; deep blue tones.
levels.3: Good exposure; clear image with minor issues.
levels.2: Basic exposure; image is faint or overexposed.
levels.1: Poor exposure; image is unclear or missing.

levels.4: Strong composition; intentional use of negative space.
levels.3: Good composition with clear intent.
levels.2: Basic composition; layout is unclear.
levels.1: Poor composition; no clear intent.

levels.4: Prints are refined with careful washing and finishing.
levels.3: Good finishing with minor issues.
levels.2: Basic finishing; some areas look unfinished.
levels.1: No evidence of refinement.

quest91.title: The Archivist's Initiation
quest91.rationale:
The Archivist's Initiation

Why it's important:
Every sketchbook begins with an artist investigation. This quest teaches you how to research an artist, analyze their work, and connect it to your own practice. It builds the foundation for all future research and critical reflection.

Skills developed:

  • Research skills (primary and secondary sources)
  • Visual analysis of artworks
  • Contextual understanding of an artist's practice
  • Personal connection to art history
  • Documentation and citation

This quest is your first step toward a professional sketchbook practice.
quest91.description:
The Archivist hands you a blank page and a single question: 'Who made something that moved you — and why?'
You must select one artist, research their work, and create a sketchbook page that presents your findings visually and critically.
requirements: Select one artist (any period, any medium)
Include at least 3 images of their work (printed or drawn)
Write a 150-word analysis covering: subject, form, context
Include one personal sketch or response inspired by their work
Cite your sources

levels.4: Deep research evident; artist's work analyzed thoroughly with clear connections to context and personal practice.
levels.3: Good research; artist's work analyzed with relevant details and context.
levels.2: Basic research; analysis is surface-level or lacks context.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear analysis or connection.

levels.4: Exceptional visual analysis; identifies form, subject, and context with insight.
levels.3: Clear analysis of form and meaning with relevant details.
levels.2: Some analysis but missing key elements or context.
levels.1: Little to no analysis; description only.

quest92.title: The Comparative Eye
quest92.rationale:
The Comparative Eye

Why it's important:
Comparative study is a core skill. This quest teaches you to analyze two works side by side, identifying similarities and differences in form, context, and meaning. It builds visual literacy and critical thinking.

Skills developed:

  • Comparative analysis
  • Formal, contextual, and conceptual analysis
  • Critical thinking and visual literacy
  • Synthesis of research
  • Personal reflection

This quest strengthens your ability to see connections across cultures, periods, and media.
quest92.description: The Archivist places two artworks before you — one from a traditional culture, one from the contemporary world. They share a theme but nothing else. You must compare them in a sketchbook spread.
requirements: Select two artworks with a shared theme (e.g., identity, nature, war)
Include images of both works
Create a comparison chart (form, context, meaning)
Write a 200-word comparative analysis
Include a personal reflection: which work speaks to you and why?

levels.4: Deep research into both works; sophisticated comparative analysis with clear connections.
levels.3: Good research; clear comparison of form, context, and meaning.
levels.2: Basic research; comparison is surface-level or incomplete.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear comparison.

levels.4: Exceptional analysis; identifies similarities and differences with insight and nuance.
levels.3: Clear analysis of both works with relevant details.
levels.2: Some analysis but missing key differences or similarities.
levels.1: Little to no analysis; description only.

quest93.title: The Process Scroll
quest93.rationale:
The Process Scroll

Why it's important:
Documenting your process is the backbone of sketchbook practice. This quest teaches you to show your thinking—from initial idea through experiments, failures, and revisions to the final work.

Skills developed:

  • Process documentation
  • Experimentation and revision
  • Critical reflection
  • Visual storytelling of your own creative journey
  • Honest self-assessment

This quest builds the habit of documenting everything, which will serve you in every future summative.
quest93.description: The Archivist wants to see how you think. You must create a sketchbook spread documenting a single artwork from start to finish. The final artwork can be simple — what matters is the journey.
requirements: Include at least 5 stages: initial idea, sketches, experiment, revision, final work
Photograph or draw each stage
Write brief annotations explaining decisions at each stage
Include one failure or mistake and what you learned from it
Reflect on what you would do differently

levels.4: Thorough documentation with clear stages, thoughtful annotations, and honest reflection.
levels.3: Good documentation with visible stages and clear annotations.
levels.2: Basic documentation; some stages missing or unclear.
levels.1: Minimal documentation; no clear process shown.

levels.4: Strong evidence of revision and refinement; significant improvement from early to final work.
levels.3: Clear evidence of revision and improvement.
levels.2: Some revision but limited improvement.
levels.1: Little to no revision or refinement.

quest94.title: The Theme Weaver
quest94.rationale:
The Theme Weaver

Why it's important:
Thematic investigation is a core skill. This quest teaches you to trace a theme through art history and contemporary practice, then connect it to your own artistic interests. It builds research depth and personal meaning-making.

Skills developed:

  • Thematic investigation
  • Contextual research across cultures and periods
  • Personal connection to art history
  • Synthesis of multiple sources
  • Visual and written analysis

This quest strengthens your ability to develop a body of work around a central idea.
quest94.description: A single thread runs through all art — but which thread will you follow? You must select a theme (e.g., 'the outsider,' 'nature's power,' 'memory') and investigate how different artists have explored it.
requirements: Select one theme
Find at least 4 artworks from different periods/cultures that address this theme
Include images and brief analysis of each
Write a reflection: what draws you to this theme?
Include one original sketch or artwork inspired by your research

levels.4: Deep research across multiple contexts; theme explored with insight and personal connection.
levels.3: Good research; clear thematic connections across artworks.
levels.2: Basic research; theme is identifiable but connections are weak.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear theme or connections.

levels.4: Exceptional analysis; identifies how each work addresses the theme with nuance.
levels.3: Clear analysis of each work with relevant details.
levels.2: Some analysis but missing key connections.
levels.1: Little to no analysis; description only.

quest95.title: The Material Witness
quest95.rationale:
The Material Witness

Why it's important:
Material and technique research deepens your understanding of how art is made. This quest teaches you to research a material or technique—its history, science, and artistic applications—then test it yourself.

Skills developed:

  • Material and technique research
  • Technical investigation
  • Experimentation documentation
  • Connecting historical practice to contemporary use
  • Hands-on testing and reflection

This quest builds your ability to make informed technical choices in your own work.
quest95.description: The Archivist hands you a mysterious material — could be gold leaf, cyanotype chemicals, or egg tempera. You must research its history, properties, and uses, then create a test piece.
requirements: Select one material or technique (e.g., fresco, batik, cyanotype)
Research: where it came from, how it works, who uses it
Include images of historical and contemporary examples
Write a 150-word summary of your findings
Create a small test piece using the material or technique
Reflect: what did you learn? What will you do with this knowledge?

levels.4: Deep research into material/technique; clear connection between history and personal testing.
levels.3: Good research; material/technique understood and tested effectively.
levels.2: Basic research; limited understanding or testing.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear understanding or test.

levels.4: Masterful handling of material/technique; test piece demonstrates strong control.
levels.3: Good control; test piece is clear and intentional.
levels.2: Basic control; test piece is rough or incomplete.
levels.1: Poor control; test piece unsuccessful or missing.

quest96.title: The Curator's Eye
quest96.rationale:
The Curator's Eye

Why it's important:
Understanding how exhibitions are curated and how context affects meaning is essential for any artist. This quest teaches you to analyze display, layout, and narrative in an exhibition or collection.

Skills developed:

  • Exhibition research and analysis
  • Curatorial thinking
  • Understanding context and display
  • Critical reflection on viewer experience
  • Proposing alternative curatorial choices

This quest connects your research skills to the presentation and reception of art.
quest96.description: The Archivist takes you to a gallery — real or virtual. You must investigate how an exhibition is curated: what's included, what's excluded, how works are arranged, and what story is being told.
requirements: Visit an exhibition (physical or virtual)
Include a floor plan or layout sketch
Select 3 artworks and analyze how they are displayed
Write a 300-word reflection: how does display affect meaning?
Propose one change you would make as curator

levels.4: Thorough research into exhibition design; insightful analysis of curatorial choices.
levels.3: Good research; clear analysis of display and context.
levels.2: Basic research; limited analysis of curatorial choices.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear analysis.

levels.4: Exceptional analysis of how display affects meaning; thoughtful proposal for alternative curation.
levels.3: Clear analysis of exhibition impact with relevant reflection.
levels.2: Some analysis but limited insight into display impact.
levels.1: Little to no analysis of exhibition or display.

quest107.title: The Paper Alchemist
quest107.rationale:
The Paper Alchemist

Why it's important:
Collage is the art of juxtaposition. It trains you to see images as materials, to compose without drawing, and to create meaning through unexpected combinations. It is one of the most accessible and expressive media available.

Skills developed:

  • Composition through shape and color
  • Juxtaposition and visual meaning-making
  • Layering and edge control
  • Selecting and editing source material
  • Working with found and recycled materials

This quest builds the compositional instincts that support all two-dimensional work.
quest107.description: The Alchemists of the Paper Guild believe that discarded images still hold magic. They hand you a stack of old magazines, newspapers, and printed scraps and ask you to create a single collage that tells a story or captures a feeling. Nothing may be drawn—only cut, torn, and arranged. The guild will judge you not on what you found, but on what you made it mean.
requirements: Create a collage using only found paper materials
Compose with intentional shape, color, and balance
Use at least 10 distinct cut or torn pieces
No drawing or painting—only paper and adhesive
Present the finished collage cleanly

levels.4: Composition is compelling and balanced; juxtaposition creates clear meaning.
levels.3: Good composition with minor imbalance.
levels.2: Basic composition; meaning is unclear or cluttered.
levels.1: Poor composition; no clear meaning or structure.

levels.4: Clean edges, intentional layering, professional finish.
levels.3: Good craftsmanship with minor rough areas.
levels.2: Some craftsmanship issues; edges or layering are messy.
levels.1: Poor craftsmanship; collage is falling apart.

quest115.title: The Transfer Artist (MVP)
quest115.rationale:
The Transfer Artist

Why it's important:
Mixed-media transfer techniques let you build images in layers—photographs, drawings, text, and paint all speaking at once. This quest teaches you to think in layers, to combine media intentionally, and to create work that rewards close looking.

Skills developed:

  • Image transfer techniques (gel medium, tape, solvent, or tracing)
  • Layering and composition across media
  • Integrating text, image, and paint
  • Material experimentation and problem-solving
  • Documentation of a complex multi-stage process

This summative proves you can combine media into a single, coherent artwork.
quest115.description: The Keepers of the Layered Archive believe that no single medium can hold a whole memory. They challenge you to create a mixed-media artwork that combines transferred images, paint, drawing, and text—layered so that each element remains visible but together they form something new. The piece must feel like a page from an old journal: dense, layered, and alive with meaning.
requirements: Create a mixed-media artwork using at least one image transfer technique
Layer at least 3 media (transfer + paint + drawing/text/collage)
Compose intentionally so each layer remains visible
Include a personal or narrative element (memory, story, theme)
Document the transfer process and layering stages

levels.4: Masterful transfer and layering; media combine seamlessly and intentionally.
levels.3: Good technique with minor issues in transfer or layering.
levels.2: Basic technique; transfer or layering is inconsistent.
levels.1: Poor technique; transfer failed or layers are muddy.

levels.4: Composition is layered and compelling; visual hierarchy is clear.
levels.3: Good composition with minor hierarchy issues.
levels.2: Basic composition; layers are cluttered or unclear.
levels.1: Poor composition; no clear organization.

levels.4: Thorough documentation of transfer tests, layering stages, and decisions.
levels.3: Good documentation with minor gaps.
levels.2: Basic documentation; missing key stages.
levels.1: No process documentation.

quest53.title: The face stealer
quest53.rationale:
The Face Stealer

Why it's important:
This quest teaches facial anatomy in 3D. Sculpting a face strengthens your understanding of proportions, planes, and expression—skills that directly improve both sculpture and drawing.

Skills developed:

  • Facial proportion and symmetry
  • Understanding of facial planes and volume
  • Texturing skin, hair, and features
  • Building expression through shape and depth
  • Fine motor control with clay tools

This quest builds a strong foundation in three-dimensional portraiture and expressive sculpture.
quest53.description:
Deep within the mountains a monster lives: Noppera-bō, the Faceless. The elders believe it was once a protector, but the loss of its face change it, now he wears the looks of anyone that cross its path. The dewarves of Etrihilleim decided its face and are looking for a courageous adventurer to craft a final face for it.
If you undertake this role you are tasked with sculpting a face using air-dry clay. Your goal is to capture expression, proportion, and surface detail. The mask should feel alive, as if it could speak.
requirements: Create a face sculpture using air-dry clay
Show correct facial proportions
Include details like eyes, nose, mouth, and ears
Add a exaggerated expression to it
Use texture and surface detail

levels.4: Face proportions are highly accurate and realistic with strong anatomy.
levels.3: Face proportions are mostly accurate with minor inconsistencies.
levels.2: Some proportional errors affect realism.
levels.1: Proportions are inaccurate and undermine the face structure.

levels.4: Highly refined details (eyes, nose, mouth, ears) with excellent surface control.
levels.3: Good detail and surface quality with minor imperfections.
levels.2: Some details are unclear or poorly defined.
levels.1: Minimal detail; surface looks unfinished.

levels.4: Expression is clear and strongly communicates emotion.
levels.3: Expression is visible and generally clear.
levels.2: Expression is weak or inconsistent.
levels.1: Expression is unclear or missing.

levels.4: Clear process documentation with strong reflection and improvement steps.
levels.3: Good documentation showing progress and decisions.
levels.2: Some documentation but lacks clarity or reflection.
levels.1: Little or no process documentation.

quest54.title: The Necklace of the Desert Moon
quest54.rationale:
The Necklace of the Desert Moon

Why it's important:
This quest focuses on precision, pattern, and cultural design. Jewelry sculpture trains your ability to work in small scale while maintaining symmetry and detail.

Skills developed:

  • Symmetry and balance in design
  • Small-scale detailing and texture
  • Pattern repetition and rhythm
  • Planning a design through sketching
  • Control of fine hand movements and clay consistency

This quest improves your precision and patience, essential for any detailed sculpting work.
quest54.description:
The Navajo people of the desert are known for their silver and turquoise jewelry, believed to carry protective power. It's beauty call for you and you decided to join then in creating their old technique.
You are asked to create a traditional jewelry sculpture using air-dry clay, inspired by Navajo designs. Your piece should reflect symmetry, pattern, and cultural respect.
requirements: Create a jewelry sculpture inspired by Navajo turquoise silver necklaces
Start with a sketch of the design. It should be in colours and seem from different angles.
Use air-dry clay
Include repeating patterns and symmetry
Use texture to simulate metal and stones
Document your process: design sketches, pattern tests, cultural reference

rubric.overall: The Necklace of the Desert Moon

levels.4: Exceptional precision with clean, detailed small-scale work.
levels.3: Good precision with clear detail.
levels.2: Some precision issues affecting clarity.
levels.1: Poor precision with unclear details.

levels.4: Strong symmetry and repeating patterns are very consistent.
levels.3: Symmetry and pattern are mostly consistent.
levels.2: Some symmetry or pattern issues.
levels.1: Patterns are inconsistent or missing.

levels.4: Sketches show strong planning and clear cultural research.
levels.3: Sketches show planning and some cultural understanding.
levels.2: Sketches are basic and lack planning.
levels.1: No planning or sketch evidence.

quest56.title: The Story Tile of the Hearth
quest56.rationale:
The Story Tile of the Hearth

Why it's important:
Low-relief sculpture teaches composition and depth in a constrained space. This quest builds storytelling through form and encourages thoughtful visual narrative.

Skills developed:

  • Relief depth and layering
  • Composition and visual storytelling
  • Texture for surface interest
  • Planning and sketching before sculpting
  • Creating clear foreground and background

This quest strengthens your ability to communicate stories through sculpture and develop visual hierarchy.
quest56.description:
A village elder has asked you to create a tile that tells a story of your life or culture. The tile will be used to decorate the community hall.
You must create a low-relief sculpture using air-dry clay, focusing on composition, depth, and texture. The scene should be clear and meaningful.
requirements: Create a triptych relief tile using air-dry clay
Start with a sketch of the design.
Include a clear scene or story
Use depth to show foreground and background
Add texture for visual interest

rubric.overall: The Story Tile of the Hearth

levels.4: Depth is strong with clear foreground/background separation.
levels.3: Depth is clear with some layering.
levels.2: Depth is inconsistent or weak.
levels.1: Depth is not clear or missing.

levels.4: Story is very clear and composition is balanced.
levels.3: Story is clear with good composition.
levels.2: Story is somewhat unclear; composition is uneven.
levels.1: Story is unclear and composition is weak.

levels.4: Sketches show strong planning and clear story development.
levels.3: Sketches show planning and some story clarity.
levels.2: Sketches are basic and incomplete.
levels.1: No planning or sketch evidence.

quest57.title: The Bound Spirit
quest57.rationale:
The Bound Spirit

Why it's important:
Wire sculpture emphasizes line, movement, and structural balance. It teaches you to build forms with minimal materials while expressing motion and emotion.

Skills developed:

  • Understanding line as structure
  • Creating dynamic movement and gesture
  • Three-dimensional composition
  • Strength and stability in construction
  • Working with tools to bend and secure wire

This quest develops your ability to build expressive forms with strong structural integrity.
quest57.description:
A trapped spirit is said to wander the realm, bound by invisible lines. To free it, you must create a wire sculpture that captures motion and emotion using only line and form.
You will bend and twist wire into a three-dimensional figure that expresses energy and movement, as if it could come to life.
requirements: Create a wire sculpture using wire and tools
it might be done in groups of two, depending on the size of the sculpture and complexity
Express motion or emotion through line
Include a stable base or structure
Use varied thickness and direction for visual interest

levels.4: Wire construction is very clean, stable, and skillful.
levels.3: Wire construction is solid with minor issues.
levels.2: Construction is weak or unstable.
levels.1: Construction is unstable and poorly built.

levels.4: Motion and gesture are strong and clearly readable.
levels.3: Motion is clear with some visual interest.
levels.2: Motion is weak or inconsistent.
levels.1: Motion is not visible or unclear.

levels.4: Structure is very stable with strong base support.
levels.3: Structure is stable with minor balance issues.
levels.2: Structure is somewhat unstable.
levels.1: Structure is unstable and falls apart.

levels.4: Process shows strong planning, tools, and steps.
levels.3: Process is documented with some detail.
levels.2: Process is incomplete or unclear.
levels.1: No process documentation.

quest58.title: The Citadel of Forms
quest58.rationale:
The Citadel of Forms

Why it's important:
This quest teaches architectural thinking in 3D. Creating buildings strengthens your understanding of mass, balance, and structural design.

Skills developed:

  • Understanding mass and volume
  • Structural design and stability
  • Architectural detail and proportion
  • Spatial planning and balance
  • Mixed media integration for strong form

This quest builds a foundation for architectural sculpture and design-focused 3D art.
quest58.description:
The ancient city of Lomakkeiden Kaupunki is built from pure geometric harmony: its arches mimicing nature; it's skyscrapers - marvels of modern craftsmanship. Inspired, you take the role of archtect and design your own building, focusing on strong structure and design.
You may also choose an abstract architectural form, but it must still show clear understanding of mass, balance, and space.
requirements: Create a building or house sculpture using mixed media
Show clear structure and architectural form
Include details such as windows, doors, or roof elements
Optional: create an abstract architectural form focusing on shapes
Document your artistic reference: which architectural style or artist are you referencing?

levels.4: Strong mass and volume with excellent 3D form clarity.
levels.3: Good mass and volume with minor issues.
levels.2: Some mass issues affect form clarity.
levels.1: Mass and volume are unclear or weak.

levels.4: Structure is very stable and well-engineered.
levels.3: Structure is stable with minor flaws.
levels.2: Structure is unstable in some areas.
levels.1: Structure is unstable and poorly designed.

levels.4: Details are precise and proportional with strong design choices.
levels.3: Details are clear and proportional.
levels.2: Details are inconsistent or disproportionate.
levels.1: Details are unclear or missing.

levels.4: Thorough documentation of architectural reference, sketches, and process.
levels.3: Good documentation with minor gaps.
levels.2: Basic documentation; missing key stages.
levels.1: No documentation or process evidence.

quest59.title: The Scales of Balance
quest59.rationale:
The Scales of Balance

Why it's important:
Balance is one of the core principles of sculpture. This quest trains you to design stable forms while maintaining visual harmony.

Skills developed:

  • Understanding physical stability and center of gravity
  • Symmetry and intentional asymmetry
  • Weight distribution and structural integrity
  • Visual balance through composition
  • Mixed media integration for support and style

This quest strengthens your ability to create sculptures that are both beautiful and structurally sound.
quest59.description:
The Temple of Equilibrium calls for a sculpture that physically represents balance. You must design a piece that feels stable and visually balanced, whether symmetrical or asymmetrical.
The sculpture should show clear control of weight and distribution, proving your mastery of this principle.
requirements: Create a sculpture that demonstrates balance
Use mixed media
Show symmetry or intentional asymmetry
Ensure the piece is stable and not top-heavy
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board

levels.4: Sculpture is extremely stable with strong weight distribution.
levels.3: Sculpture is stable with minor balance issues.
levels.2: Sculpture is somewhat unstable or top-heavy.
levels.1: Sculpture is unstable and unsafe.

levels.4: Visual balance is strong and intentional, with excellent composition.
levels.3: Visual balance is clear with good composition.
levels.2: Visual balance is weak or inconsistent.
levels.1: Visual balance is unclear or lacking.

levels.4: Strong planning and documentation showing design decisions.
levels.3: Good planning and process evidence.
levels.2: Limited planning or unclear process.
levels.1: No process evidence.

quest60.title: The Duel of Light and Shadow
quest60.rationale:
The Duel of Light and Shadow

Why it's important:
Contrast creates drama in sculpture. This quest teaches how to use texture, thickness, and shape to emphasize opposing elements.

Skills developed:

  • Textural contrast (smooth vs rough)
  • Form contrast (thick vs thin)
  • Visual impact through opposing elements
  • Creative use of material differences
  • Understanding how light interacts with surface

This quest improves your ability to design sculptures with strong visual tension and clarity.
quest60.description:
A wizard of shadows challenges you to create a sculpture that shows strong contrast between smooth and rough, thick and thin, light and dark.
Your work should clearly display opposing elements, making the difference visible and powerful.
requirements: Create a sculpture demonstrating contrast
Use different textures and shapes
Include a mix of thick and thin elements
Make contrasts clearly visible
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board

rubric.overall: The Duel of Light and Shadow

levels.4: Contrast is dramatic and intentional with strong texture variety.
levels.3: Contrast is clear with good texture variety.
levels.2: Contrast is weak or inconsistent.
levels.1: Little to no contrast visible.

levels.4: Contrast creates strong visual drama and clarity.
levels.3: Contrast creates good visual impact.
levels.2: Contrast is unclear or weak.
levels.1: No visual impact.

levels.4: Process shows intentional contrast decisions and planning.
levels.3: Process shows planning with some clarity.
levels.2: Process is limited or unclear.
levels.1: No process evidence.

quest61.title: The Heart of the Statue
quest61.rationale:
The Heart of the Statue

Why it's important:
Creating a clear focal point teaches visual hierarchy and intentional design. This quest trains you to guide the viewer's eye and emphasize meaning through sculpture.

Skills developed:

  • Creating emphasis through size, texture, or detail
  • Designing visual hierarchy
  • Balancing supporting forms
  • Planning composition for impact
  • Clarity of storytelling through focal points

This quest strengthens your ability to design sculptures with strong emotional and visual focus.
quest61.description:
The Shrine of Focus demands a sculpture with a clear focal point. Your challenge is to create a piece where one area draws the viewer's attention first.
Use shape, size, texture, or detail to create emphasis and guide the eye.
requirements: Create a sculpture with clear emphasis
Use one strong focal point
Use size, texture, or detail to emphasize
Support the focal point with surrounding forms
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board

levels.4: Focal point is very strong and immediately draws attention.
levels.3: Focal point is clear and effective.
levels.2: Focal point is weak or unclear.
levels.1: No clear focal point.

levels.4: Supporting elements enhance the focal point perfectly.
levels.3: Supporting elements generally support the focal point.
levels.2: Supporting elements are inconsistent.
levels.1: Supporting elements distract from focal point.

levels.4: Planning shows strong intention and clear visual hierarchy.
levels.3: Planning shows good intention.
levels.2: Planning is minimal or unclear.
levels.1: No planning evidence.

quest62.title: The Dance of the Wind
quest62.rationale:
The Dance of the Wind

Why it's important:
Movement in sculpture brings life and energy. This quest teaches you how to suggest motion through shape, line, and rhythm in 3D.

Skills developed:

  • Dynamic composition and flow
  • Gesture and rhythm in form
  • Working with curves and directional lines
  • Balance and stability in dynamic shapes
  • Creating movement that reads from multiple angles

This quest builds your ability to create sculptures that feel alive and fluid.
quest62.description:
A wind spirit wants to be seen in solid form. You must create a sculpture that suggests movement—flowing lines, twisting shapes, or dynamic poses.
The piece should feel alive, as if it could shift with the breeze.
requirements: Create a sculpture that suggests movement
Use flowing lines or dynamic shapes
Show direction and rhythm
Make the movement clear from different angles
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board

levels.4: Movement is strong and fluid from all angles.
levels.3: Movement is clear and readable.
levels.2: Movement is weak or inconsistent.
levels.1: Movement is unclear or absent.

levels.4: Forms show strong rhythm and dynamic composition.
levels.3: Forms show good rhythm.
levels.2: Rhythm is inconsistent.
levels.1: Rhythm is absent.

levels.4: Process shows clear planning and movement decisions.
levels.3: Process shows planning with some clarity.
levels.2: Process is limited or unclear.
levels.1: No process evidence.

quest63.title: The Echoing Repetition
quest63.rationale:
The Echoing Repetition

Why it's important:
Repetition creates rhythm and harmony in sculpture. This quest teaches pattern, structure, and consistency while building visual movement.

Skills developed:

  • Pattern creation and repetition
  • Visual rhythm and flow
  • Consistency in repeated forms
  • Balancing repetition with variety
  • Creating sculptural unity through repeated elements

This quest strengthens your ability to create cohesive sculptures with strong visual rhythm.
quest63.description:
A bard of stone wants to hear rhythm through form. You must create a sculpture that uses repetition and pattern to create visual rhythm.
The piece should feel like a repeated beat or pulse, guiding the viewer through its shapes.
requirements: Create a sculpture showing rhythm
Use repeated shapes or patterns
Create a sense of movement through repetition
Maintain visual consistency
The piece should be done on a 10x10 piece of board

levels.4: Patterns are very consistent and rhythm is strong.
levels.3: Patterns are clear and consistent.
levels.2: Patterns are inconsistent or weak.
levels.1: Patterns are missing or unclear.

levels.4: Rhythm is strong and creates unity throughout the sculpture.
levels.3: Rhythm is clear and supports unity.
levels.2: Rhythm is weak or uneven.
levels.1: No rhythm or unity.

levels.4: Process shows intentional planning of pattern and rhythm.
levels.3: Process shows planning with some clarity.
levels.2: Process is limited or unclear.
levels.1: No process evidence.

quest68.title: The Master Forgemaster's Covenant
quest68.rationale:
The Master Forgemaster's Covenant

Why it's important:
This summative team quest challenges artists to collaborate in designing and constructing a cosplay build using EVA foam. By working in small teams, students must communicate ideas, divide responsibilities, and refine a shared vision while demonstrating craftsmanship and technical growth.

Skills developed:

  • Collaborative planning and problem-solving
  • Experimentation with materials and techniques
  • Three-dimensional construction and craftsmanship
  • Revision, refinement, and process documentation
quest68.description:
No great armor is forged alone.
In this final trial, a small guild of artisans must work together to design and construct a cosplay build using EVA foam. Teams of no more than three must coordinate planning, fabrication, and refinement to produce a cohesive final piece.
requirements: Work in a team of no more than three students
Collaboratively design a cosplay build using sketches or patterns
Experiment with EVA foam techniques during construction
Construct a complete and cohesive cosplay element or set
Refine the final work based on testing, feedback, and team reflection
Document the process, including individual contributions

levels.4: Team demonstrates exceptional collaboration with a unified vision and balanced contributions.
levels.3: Team collaborates effectively with clear shared planning.
levels.2: Collaboration is uneven; roles or communication are inconsistent.
levels.1: Minimal collaboration; work appears fragmented.

levels.4: Exceptional craftsmanship and control of EVA foam techniques throughout the build.
levels.3: Effective use of techniques with solid construction.
levels.2: Inconsistent technique application; structural or finish issues present.
levels.1: Limited understanding of EVA foam techniques.

levels.4: Extensive refinement and revisions significantly improve the final build.
levels.3: Clear refinement and revisions enhance the cosplay piece.
levels.2: Some refinement; revisions are limited.
levels.1: Little evidence of refinement or revision.

levels.4: Thorough documentation clearly shows development, decisions, and individual roles.
levels.3: Documentation shows key stages and contributions.
levels.2: Limited documentation with unclear roles or missing stages.
levels.1: Minimal or no documentation provided.

quest70.title: The Animist's Awakening
quest70.rationale:
The Animist's Awakening

Why it's important:
This summative quest bridges functional design with artistic expression. Redesigning an everyday object teaches students to analyze form, function, and aesthetics while developing creative problem-solving skills. The challenge requires both technical 3D construction and conceptual thinking about how objects 'live' in our world.

Skills developed:

  • Analytical observation of existing objects
  • Conceptual redesign and creative transformation
  • 3D construction with mixed media
  • Functional and aesthetic balance
  • Process documentation from research to final product

This quest prepares students for design thinking and encourages them to see the artistic potential in everyday items.
quest70.description:
In the Workshop of Awakened Forms, the old tinkerer Móðir sits surrounded by mundane objects she calls 'sleeping spirits.' She believes every manufactured thing holds a latent personality, waiting to be revealed through redesign.

She hands you an ordinary, mass-produced object—a chair, lamp, table, or similar. 'This one,' she whispers, 'dreams of being more than it is. It yearns for a second life, a truer form.'

Your task is to listen to the object's hidden character and redesign it into something that expresses its soul. You must respect its original function while transforming its appearance, materiality, and presence entirely. The final piece should feel like the object has awakened, revealing what it was always meant to be.
requirements: Select one ordinary, mass-produced object as your starting point
Research and analyze its current form, function, and manufacturing
Create a completely redesigned version that maintains its core function
Use mixed media (clay, wire, found objects, EVA foam, etc.) for construction
Include a written statement explaining your redesign concept
Document your entire process: research → sketches → prototypes → final piece

levels.4: Deep research into original object's design; sophisticated concept connecting form, function, and transformation.
levels.3: Clear research and concept development; logical connection between original and redesign.
levels.2: Basic research; concept is simplistic or unclear in its transformation logic.
levels.1: Minimal research; no clear conceptual foundation for the redesign.

levels.4: Exceptional craftsmanship; materials used intentionally and skillfully; construction is solid and refined.
levels.3: Good craftsmanship; materials used effectively; construction is mostly solid.
levels.2: Adequate craftsmanship; some technical issues with materials or construction.
levels.1: Poor craftsmanship; construction is unstable or materials misused.

levels.4: Redesign successfully balances radical aesthetics with maintained/improved function; form follows concept.
levels.3: Good balance between new form and original function; design is coherent.
levels.2: Uneven balance; either form or function suffers in the transformation.
levels.1: Poor design; function is lost or form is incoherent.

levels.4: Sophisticated analysis of original object's design flaws/opportunities; insightful reflection on transformation choices.
levels.3: Clear analysis and reflection; understands strengths/weaknesses of redesign.
levels.2: Basic analysis; reflection lacks depth or specificity.
levels.1: Minimal analysis or reflection; cannot articulate design decisions.

quest71.title: The Dreamweaver's Gambit
quest71.rationale:
The Dreamweaver's Gambit

Why it's important:
This quest combines art history, technical craft, and conceptual translation. Needle felting requires patience, precision, and spatial thinking while reproducing a 2D painting in 3D wool teaches students to analyze color, composition, and texture in new dimensions. The challenge of translating brushstrokes into wool fibers develops both observational skills and material mastery.

Skills developed:

  • Art historical analysis and interpretation
  • Needle felting technique and wool manipulation
  • Color theory application with fiber materials
  • Spatial translation from 2D to 3D form
  • Patience and precision in craft execution

This quest demonstrates how traditional crafts can reinterpret fine art, bridging historical and contemporary making practices.
quest71.description:
The village of Stillaheim is haunted by Mara, the Nightmare Weaver—a creature who traps minds in restless sleep by unraveling their memories into tangled wool. Her power grows from stolen dreams, which she hangs as spectral tapestries in her lair.

Only one art can counter her: the ancient craft of felting, which binds loose fibers into solid truth. The elders have discovered Mara's weakness—she cannot bear to see dreams made permanent, rendered with such conviction that they cannot be undone.

You are tasked with selecting a famous painting whose emotional power matches Mara's dark artistry. Through needle felting, you must recreate this masterpiece in wool, stitch by meticulous stitch. Your felted reproduction must capture not just the image, but the painting's soul—its color harmonies, its emotional weight, its very essence made tangible. Only a work of such crafted truth can unravel Mara's nightmares and restore peaceful sleep.
requirements: Select one famous painting from any art movement or period
Research the painting's composition, color palette, and emotional impact
Create a needle-felted reproduction using wool fibers
Include a color study showing your wool color selections matching the original
Present both the original painting reference and your 3D felted version
Write a brief analysis explaining your translation choices from paint to wool

levels.4: Deep research into painting's context; sophisticated understanding of style, technique, and emotional intent translated into felted form.
levels.3: Clear research; good understanding of painting's elements effectively translated to wool medium.
levels.2: Basic research; some elements misunderstood or poorly translated between mediums.
levels.1: Minimal research; poor understanding of original artwork's qualities.

levels.4: Exceptional felting control; wool density, color blending, and texture masterfully recreate painting's effects.
levels.3: Good technical control; clear effort to match painting's qualities with wool techniques.
levels.2: Adequate technique; inconsistencies in wool application or texture.
levels.1: Poor technical control; felted work lacks refinement or cohesion.

levels.4: Brilliant translation from 2D to 3D; captures painting's essence while exploring wool's unique textural possibilities.
levels.3: Clear translation; reproduces key elements accurately in felted form.
levels.2: Partial translation; some elements lost or misinterpreted in medium change.
levels.1: Poor translation; little connection between original and felted version.

levels.4: Masterful composition replication; color matching and wool blending create harmonious, balanced felted artwork.
levels.3: Good composition and color harmony; mostly accurate to original painting.
levels.2: Uneven composition; color choices deviate significantly from original.
levels.1: Poor composition; color harmony lacking or incorrect.

quest76.title: The Sculptor's Menagerie
quest76.rationale:
The Sculptor's Menagerie

Why it's important:
This summative quest introduces students to figurative sculpture through imaginative creature design. By working with air-dry clay over wire armature, students learn essential 3D construction principles: structural support, additive/subtractive techniques, surface texturing, and spatial thinking. The fantastical subject matter encourages creative risk-taking while still demanding anatomical believability and technical craftsmanship.

Skills developed:

  • Armature construction for structural stability
  • 3D form building and proportion
  • Surface texturing techniques (fur, scales, skin)
  • Understanding balance and weight distribution
  • Creative anatomy and creature design

This quest builds confidence in sculptural practice and prepares students for more complex figurative work.
quest76.description:
Deep in the Whispering Woods, the last Keeper of the Menagerie tends to creatures that exist only in dreams and stories. But the Keeper is aging, and their magic is fading. Soon, these fantastical beasts will be forgotten unless someone can preserve them in solid form.

You have been summoned to the Keeper's workshop, where sketches of impossible creatures line the walls—griffins with feathered serpents' tails, foxes with crystalline antlers, turtles with moss-grown shells. Your task is to choose one creature from the Keeper's sketches—or imagine your own—and bring it to life as a small sculpture.

Using wire to build its hidden skeleton and clay to give it flesh and texture, you must create a creature so convincing that it could almost breathe. The Keeper will know you have succeeded when your sculpture feels balanced, textured, and alive—a permanent guardian for the fading menagerie.
requirements: Design an original fantastical creature or select one from provided references
Create a wire armature that supports the creature's pose and weight
Build the form using air-dry clay, showing clear anatomical understanding
Apply surface textures that suggest fur, scales, feathers, or skin
Ensure the sculpture is structurally stable and balanced
Document your process with photos showing armature, construction stages, and final piece
Include a brief artist statement explaining your creature's inspiration and design choices

levels.4: Exceptional craftsmanship; armature is expertly built and fully integrated; clay work is smooth, refined, and shows masterful control.
levels.3: Good construction; armature supports form effectively; clay work is clean with minor surface imperfections.
levels.2: Adequate construction; some structural weaknesses or rough areas; armature may be partially visible or unstable.
levels.1: Poor construction; armature insufficient or missing; clay work is rough and uncontrolled.

levels.4: Creature anatomy is highly convincing and believable within its fantasy context; proportions are intentional and balanced from all angles.
levels.3: Clear anatomical understanding; proportions are mostly consistent and form reads well.
levels.2: Some anatomical confusion; proportions are inconsistent or form is unclear from certain angles.
levels.1: Poor anatomical understanding; form lacks coherence and proportion.

levels.4: Textures are masterfully rendered and clearly communicate surface qualities (fur, scales, etc.); details enhance the creature's believability and character.
levels.3: Effective texture application; surface qualities are identifiable and consistent.
levels.2: Basic texture attempts; surface feels generic or textures are unclear.
levels.1: Little to no surface texture; finish is flat and unfinished.

levels.4: Highly original creature design with thoughtful concept development; documentation thoroughly shows process from armature to final piece.
levels.3: Clear creative concept; documentation shows key stages with good detail.
levels.2: Basic concept; documentation is incomplete or lacks clarity.
levels.1: Minimal concept development; little to no process documentation.

quest77.title: The Weaver's Legacy
quest77.rationale:
The Weaver's Legacy

Why it's important:
This culminating quest challenges students to bridge 2D design and 3D construction by creating a wearable piece of art. Students must synthesize figure drawing, textile understanding, and sculptural thinking to transform a flat design into a three-dimensional garment. The process requires planning, problem-solving, and craftsmanship while allowing for immense creative expression. This quest prepares students for costume design, fashion construction, and wearable art practices.

Skills developed:

  • Translating 2D designs into 3D forms
  • Pattern making and construction techniques
  • Material selection and textile manipulation
  • Wearable structure and fit considerations
  • Integrated design process from concept to finished piece

This quest demonstrates mastery of the full design cycle and the ability to bring imagined clothing into physical reality.
quest77.description:
In the mountain loom - halls of the Weaver's Guild -, an ancient tradition continues: each year, apprentices must create a single garment that tells a story. Not just any story—a story woven, stitched, and shaped into fabric that can be worn.

The Guild Master, an elderly woman named Elara who has woven garments for queens and kings, has chosen you for the final test. She places before you sketches from throughout history: a warrior's cloak, a dancer's dress, a scholar's robe. 'Choose your inspiration,' she says, 'but do not copy. Listen to what the fabric wants to become.'

Your task is to create an original piece of clothing—a garment that can be worn, displayed on a form, or hung as sculpture. It must begin with the design skills you demonstrated in your fashion sketchbook, showing thoughtful development from 2D concept to 3D reality. Through fabric, stitching, and structure, you will weave your own legacy into the Guild's collection.
requirements: Complete The Fashionista's Sketchbook as a prerequisite (designs must include the piece you plan to construct)
Select one design from your fashion sketchbook collection to bring into 3D form
Create detailed construction plans including pattern pieces and material lists
Construct a wearable garment or garment equivalent using appropriate fabrics and techniques
Demonstrate understanding of fit, structure, and material behavior
Document your full process: initial design → pattern development → material selection → construction stages → final piece
Present the finished garment on a form, mannequin, or model with your original sketchbook for comparison

levels.4: Exceptional connection between sketchbook design and final garment; thoughtful adaptations show sophisticated problem-solving and material understanding.
levels.3: Clear translation from 2D to 3D; design intent is preserved with appropriate material adaptations.
levels.2: Some connection between sketch and garment; translation challenges were partially resolved.
levels.1: Weak connection between design and final piece; translation appears unplanned or unsuccessful.

levels.4: Masterful construction with professional-level stitching, finishing, and structural integrity; garment is well-finished inside and out.
levels.3: Good construction with clean stitching and solid structure; minor finishing issues present.
levels.2: Adequate construction; some structural weaknesses or visible flaws in craftsmanship.
levels.1: Poor construction; garment is unstable, unfinished, or poorly assembled.

levels.4: Exceptional material choices that enhance design intent; fabrics are manipulated skillfully to achieve desired effects and fit.
levels.3: Good material choices appropriate to design; fabrics are handled effectively.
levels.2: Basic material choices; some issues with fabric behavior or manipulation.
levels.1: Poor material choices; fabrics work against design or are mishandled.

levels.4: Exceptional attention to form and fit; garment functions as intended with strong sculptural or wearable presence.
levels.3: Good form and fit; garment achieves intended silhouette and function.
levels.2: Adequate form; some fit or structural issues affect intended appearance.
levels.1: Poor form; garment does not achieve intended silhouette or function.

quest81.title: The Foamsmith's Apprentice
quest81.rationale:
The Foamsmith's Apprentice

Why it's important:
EVA foam is the primary material for modern cosplay construction. This quest teaches the fundamental techniques of cutting, shaping, sealing, and painting foam—skills that directly transfer to armor, weapons, and props. Without mastering these basics, students will struggle with the collaborative cosplay summative.

Skills developed:

  • Safe cutting techniques with hobby knives
  • Heat shaping with heat guns
  • Contact cement application and seam hiding
  • PlastiDip/Komba sealing methods
  • Acrylic painting on flexible surfaces
  • Pattern transfer from 2D to 3D forms

This quest builds the technical foundation required for the Master Forgemaster's Covenant.
quest81.description:
In the workshop of Old Man Kaelen, the kingdom's finest armorsmith has retired to teaching the sacred craft of foam. 'Metal is heavy and unkind,' he grumbles, handing you a sheet of EVA foam. 'But foam... foam can become anything if you learn its secrets.'

Your task is to create basic shapes using using EVA foam, demonstrating all five stages of foamsmithing: pattern, cut, shape, seal, and paint.
requirements: Create a cube, a convex shape and a half circle piece from EVA foam
Demonstrate at least one curved/domed shape achieved through heat forming
Show clean seams with glue (no visible gaps)
Apply proper sealing (PlastiDip, white glue or heat sealing) before painting
Finish with acrylic paint showing base color, shading, and at least one highlight or weathering effect

levels.4: Clean, precise cuts; perfect heat-formed curves; invisible seams; professional-level finishing.
levels.3: Good cuts with minor rough edges; clear heat shaping; seams are visible but clean.
levels.2: Inconsistent cuts; heat shaping attempted but uneven; seams are messy or gaping.
levels.1: Poor cutting; no effective heat shaping; seams falling apart or not attempted.

levels.4: Professional paint job with smooth coverage, intentional shading/highlights, and convincing material effect (metal, leather, etc.).
levels.3: Good paint coverage with basic shading; material effect is readable.
levels.2: Uneven paint; no shading or highlights; material effect is unclear.
levels.1: Poor paint application; no finish work.

quest82.title: The Maskmaker's Ritual
quest82.rationale:
The Maskmaker's Ritual

Why it's important:
Mask-making combines sculpture, painting, and wearable art. It teaches facial structure, surface building, and the translation of character into 3D form. Papier mâché is inexpensive, forgiving, and highly versatile—ideal for large-scale, lightweight construction.

Skills developed:

  • Armature building and mold-making
  • Layering and surface building
  • Symmetry and facial proportion
  • Painting and finishing 3D surfaces
  • Wearable structure and comfort considerations
quest82.description:
In the Village of Masks, every face tells a story. The elders have commissioned you to create a mask for the Festival of Ancestors—a mask that captures a spirit, emotion, or character.
Using papier mâché, you must build a wearable mask that is both structurally sound and visually compelling.
requirements: Create a wearable papier mâché mask
Build a mold or armature to support the form
Apply at least 4-6 layers of papier mâché
Show clear facial structure or character design
Paint and finish the mask with intentional color and detail
Ensure the mask is wearable (eye holes, comfortable fit)

levels.4: Masterful layering, smooth surface, and professional finish.
levels.3: Good layering and surface with minor imperfections.
levels.2: Basic layering; surface is uneven or unfinished.
levels.1: Poor construction; mask is fragile or incomplete.

levels.4: Highly refined design with strong character and detail.
levels.3: Clear design with good attention to form and finish.
levels.2: Basic design; some areas lack clarity or refinement.
levels.1: Little refinement; design is unclear or unfinished.

levels.4: Thorough documentation of mold-making, layering, and finishing.
levels.3: Good documentation of key stages.
levels.2: Limited documentation or missing stages.
levels.1: No process documentation.

quest83.title: The Paperwright's Colossus
quest83.rationale:
The Paperwright's Colossus

Why it's important:
Large-scale papier mâché teaches structural engineering, proportion, and the transformation of humble materials into monumental form. This is distinctly different from clay and foam because it requires building hollow forms and managing weight.

Skills developed:

  • Armature construction for large forms
  • Hollow form building and structural integrity
  • Proportion and scale management
  • Surface finishing and painting on curved forms
  • Problem-solving with lightweight materials
quest83.description:
The Paperwrights of the Eastern Guild are famous for creating towering sculptures from nothing but paper and paste. They challenge you to build a sculpture that stands at least 30cm tall, using papier mâché over a wire or cardboard armature.
The subject may be a creature, figure, or abstract form.
requirements: Create a papier mâché sculpture (minimum 30cm in one dimension)
Build a wire or cardboard armature
Apply at least 5-8 layers of papier mâché
Show clear form and proportion
Paint and finish with intentional color and detail
Ensure structural stability (free-standing or wall-mounted)

levels.4: Masterful construction; smooth surface; excellent structural integrity.
levels.3: Good construction with minor surface or structural issues.
levels.2: Basic construction; uneven surface or weak structure.
levels.1: Poor construction; unstable or incomplete.

levels.4: Form is highly convincing; proportions are accurate.
levels.3: Clear form with mostly accurate proportions.
levels.2: Form is unclear; proportions are inconsistent.
levels.1: Form is unrecognizable; proportions are incorrect.

levels.4: Thorough documentation of armature, layering, and finishing.
levels.3: Good documentation of key stages.
levels.2: Limited documentation.
levels.1: No process documentation.

quest84.title: The Kinusaiga Master's Trial
quest84.rationale:
The Kinusaiga Master's Trial

Why it's important:
Kinusaiga is a Japanese technique of creating pictures by cutting fabric into shapes and tucking them into grooves carved into a wooden board. No sewing or loom required — just fabric, a board, and a craft knife. It teaches color composition, precision, and the translation of 2D design into textile form.

Skills developed:

  • Design transfer and composition planning
  • Precision cutting with craft knife
  • Color and pattern selection in fabric
  • Groove carving and fabric tucking
  • Patience and fine motor control
quest84.description: In the textile villages of Yukonyama, kinusaiga artists transform discarded kimono fabric into stunning pictures. The village elder challenges you to create a kinusaiga piece that captures a scene or image using fabric scraps, a wooden board, and a craft knife.
requirements: Create a kinusaiga textile painting
Design must be transferred to a foam or wooden board
Use at least 4 different fabrics/colors
Carve grooves to define shapes
Tuck fabric into grooves to fill the design
Finish with a clean border or frame

levels.4: Masterful cutting and tucking; smooth fabric placement; professional finish.
levels.3: Good technique; clean cuts with minor fabric lifting.
levels.2: Basic technique; uneven cuts or fabric not fully tucked.
levels.1: Poor technique; fabric loose or design unclear.

levels.4: Exceptional composition; fabric choices enhance the design.
levels.3: Good composition with clear color harmony.
levels.2: Basic composition; color choices inconsistent.
levels.1: Poor composition; colors clash or design is unclear.

levels.4: Thorough planning; design transfer, fabric selection, and execution documented.
levels.3: Good planning and documentation.
levels.2: Limited planning; process unclear.
levels.1: No planning or documentation.

quest88.title: The Mosaicist's Mandala
quest88.rationale:
The Mosaicist's Mandala

Why it's important:
Mosaic teaches color theory, pattern, and patience while working with fragmented materials. It bridges 2D and 3D and is distinct from relief and tile work.

Skills developed:

  • Color theory with fragmented materials
  • Pattern and repetition
  • Patience and precision
  • Composition with tesserae
  • Grouting and finishing
quest88.description: The Mosaicist's Guild preserves the ancient art of arranging small pieces into grand images. You must create a mosaic using tile, glass, or found materials.
requirements: Create a mosaic artwork (minimum 15x15cm)
Use at least 3 different colors of tesserae
Show pattern, image, or abstract design
Grout and finish the piece
Ensure all pieces are securely attached

levels.4: Masterful placement and grouting; clean, secure finish.
levels.3: Good technique; pieces are secure with minor gaps.
levels.2: Basic technique; some pieces loose or grouting uneven.
levels.1: Poor technique; pieces falling off or grout messy.

levels.4: Exceptional composition; color choices enhance the design.
levels.3: Good composition with clear color harmony.
levels.2: Basic composition; color choices inconsistent.
levels.1: Poor composition; colors clash or design unclear.

quest97.title: The One Who Cares
quest97.rationale:
The One Who Cares

Why it's important:
An artist's tools are the extension of their hand. Brushes, palettes, pails, rulers, electric erasers, and brush cases are shared resources that must last the whole semester for every student. Learning to clean, store, and maintain them is part of being a responsible artist — and it directly affects the quality of your work.

Skills developed:

  • Responsible stewardship of shared materials
  • Proper cleaning and storage of brushes and tools
  • Routine maintenance habits
  • Respect for communal studio resources
quest97.description: The Guild of Keepers watches over the tools of Artheim. You are entrusted with the materials given to you at the beginning of the semester: brushes, pail, palette, rulers, electric eraser, and brush case. Demonstrate that you can care for them properly so they remain in good condition throughout the term.
requirements: Clean your brushes thoroughly after every use and reshape the bristles
Wash and dry your pail and palette after each session
Keep rulers clean and free of paint or graphite buildup
Clean the electric eraser and empty its shavings regularly
Store all brushes in your brush case when not in use
Keep all materials in good condition for the full semester. Remember that any damaged or lost aterial must be replaced

levels.4: All materials are consistently clean, well-maintained, and properly stored. Brushes are reshaped after every use, pail and palette are washed, rulers and eraser are kept free of residue, and the brush case is used correctly. Sets an example for others.
levels.3: Materials are generally well cared for with occasional reminders. Most items are clean and stored properly, but one area (e.g., brush reshaping or ruler cleaning) is inconsistent.
levels.2: Materials show signs of neglect. Brushes are sometimes left uncleaned, pail or palette is not washed, or tools are not returned to the brush case. Requires frequent reminders.
levels.1: Materials are poorly maintained. Brushes are damaged or left dirty, tools are lost or misused, and the brush case is not used. Shows little regard for shared resources.

links.type: How to clean and store paintbrushes

quest105.title: The Cardboard Architect
quest105.rationale:
The Cardboard Architect

Why it's important:
Cardboard is the most accessible building material in the world, and it teaches structural thinking without the expense of wood or foam. Every joint, every fold, every load-bearing edge is a lesson in engineering.

Skills developed:

  • Structural thinking and load distribution
  • Joining techniques (tabs, slots, layering, glue)
  • Scale and proportion
  • Planning and measuring
  • Translating 2D design into 3D form

This builds the engineering mindset that underlies all 3D work.
quest105.description: The Paperwrights of the Eastern Guild have no wood and no stone—only cardboard, glue, and stubbornness. They challenge you to build a structure that stands on its own: a tower, a bridge, a small house, or an abstract form. It must be strong enough to survive a gentle nudge and beautiful enough to earn a place in their gallery of humble materials.
requirements: Build a freestanding cardboard structure
Use at least two joining techniques (tabs, slots, layering, or glue)
Show clear structural thinking (load-bearing, balanced)
Keep scale and proportion intentional
Finish the surface with paint, paper, or mixed media

levels.4: Excellent joins and structural integrity; clean, intentional craftsmanship.
levels.3: Good joins with minor structural weaknesses.
levels.2: Basic joins; structure is unstable or messy.
levels.1: Poor joins; structure collapses or falls apart.

levels.4: Strong composition and clear spatial logic; structure reads clearly from all angles.
levels.3: Good organization with minor spatial issues.
levels.2: Uneven organization; form is unclear in places.
levels.1: Poor organization; form is confusing.

quest106.title: The Soap Carving
quest106.rationale:
The Soap Carving

Why it's important:
Subtractive sculpture is the opposite of building up. You must remove material to reveal form, which requires planning, patience, and a tolerance for mistakes. Soap is forgiving and cheap—perfect for learning the mindset.

Skills developed:

  • Subtractive carving and planning
  • Understanding negative space
  • Tool control (knife, spoon, toothpick)
  • Form simplification
  • Patience and refinement

This quest introduces the subtractive mindset that underlies plaster, wood, and stone carving.
quest106.description: The Carvers of the Soft Stone Order believe that all sculpture begins with what you remove. They hand you a bar of soap and a simple tool and ask you to carve a form—an animal, a face, a geometric shape, or anything you can name. The soap will fight you. It will crumble. But if you plan before you cut, you will learn the oldest lesson in sculpture.
requirements: Carve a recognizable form from a bar of soap
Plan the form before cutting (sketch first)
Use at least 2 different carving tools
Show clear form and simplified detail
Finish the surface smoothly where intended

levels.4: Confident, controlled carving; form is clean and well-defined.
levels.3: Good carving with minor rough areas.
levels.2: Basic carving; form is unclear or uneven.
levels.1: Poor carving; form is unrecognizable.

levels.4: Highly refined surface and form; intentional detail throughout.
levels.3: Mostly refined with minor unresolved areas.
levels.2: Some refinement; several areas look unfinished.
levels.1: Little evidence of refinement.

quest112.title: The Kinetic Sculpture (MVP)
quest112.rationale:
The Kinetic Sculpture

Why it's important:
A sculpture that moves is a sculpture that breathes. Kinetic art combines engineering, balance, and aesthetics in a way no static piece can. This quest challenges you to make movement itself the subject.

Skills developed:

  • Balance, counterweight, and motion mechanics
  • Structural planning and prototyping
  • Composition in motion (viewed from multiple angles)
  • Material selection for weight and durability
  • Refinement through testing and revision

This summative proves you can engineer beauty that moves.
quest112.description: The Windcallers of the Open Sky believe that art should not sit still. They challenge you to build a kinetic sculpture—a mobile, a spinner, a pendulum, a rotating form—that moves gracefully and remains balanced. The piece must be beautiful in motion and at rest. The Windcallers will judge not just the object, but the dance it performs when the air touches it.
requirements: Create a kinetic sculpture that moves freely
Demonstrate balance and counterweight planning
Build with durable, appropriate materials (wire, wood, foam, found objects)
Document prototyping and testing stages
Refine the piece based on how it moves

levels.4: Masterful construction; movement is smooth and structurally sound.
levels.3: Good construction with minor mechanical issues.
levels.2: Basic construction; movement is jerky or unstable.
levels.1: Poor construction; sculpture does not move properly.

levels.4: Excellent balance and composition; piece is beautiful from all angles.
levels.3: Good balance with minor visual or physical issues.
levels.2: Uneven balance; composition is weak.
levels.1: Poor balance; piece is unstable.

levels.4: Extensive testing and refinement; piece moves beautifully.
levels.3: Clear refinement with minor improvements needed.
levels.2: Limited refinement; movement feels unpolished.
levels.1: No evidence of refinement.

quest113.title: The Light Sculpture (MVP)
quest113.rationale:
The Light Sculpture

Why it's important:
Light transforms sculpture. A form that looks heavy in daylight can become ethereal when lit from within. This quest teaches you to design with light and shadow as active materials, not just illumination.

Skills developed:

  • Working with translucency and opacity
  • Shadow as a compositional element
  • Integrating light sources into 3D form
  • Material experimentation (wire, paper, plastic, fabric)
  • Mood and atmosphere through lighting

This summative proves you can make light itself a sculpture material.
quest113.description: The Luminary Circle guards a secret: light is not just illumination—it is a material. They challenge you to build a sculpture that incorporates light (LED, candle, string light, or ambient light through translucency). The piece must transform when lit, revealing shadows and layers invisible in the dark. The Circle will judge whether your sculpture feels alive when the light enters it.
requirements: Create a sculpture that incorporates a light source or translucent material
Design the piece so light and shadow are part of the composition
Use materials that interact with light (paper, plastic, fabric, wire, glass)
Test the piece in both lit and unlit conditions
Document the lighting effect through photographs

levels.4: Masterful integration of light and structure; the piece transforms dramatically when lit.
levels.3: Good integration with clear light effect.
levels.2: Basic integration; light effect is weak or unplanned.
levels.1: Poor integration; light is an afterthought.

levels.4: Composition is powerful in both lit and unlit states; mood is strong.
levels.3: Good composition with clear atmosphere.
levels.2: Uneven composition; mood is inconsistent.
levels.1: Poor composition; no clear atmosphere.

levels.4: Extensive testing; light and shadow are refined to perfection.
levels.3: Clear refinement with minor adjustments needed.
levels.2: Limited refinement; lighting feels unresolved.
levels.1: No refinement or testing evident.

quest114.title: The Miniature World (MVP)
quest114.rationale:
The Miniature World

Why it's important:
A diorama is a complete world in miniature. It requires you to think about scale, narrative, environment, and construction all at once—skills that transfer to film sets, game design, and installation art.

Skills developed:

  • Scale and proportion in miniature
  • Environmental storytelling
  • Mixed-media construction (clay, cardboard, foam, found objects)
  • Lighting and atmospheric design
  • Planning a complete scene from scratch

This summative proves you can build a world and tell its story without words.
quest114.description: The Cartographers of the Shrunken Realm have discovered that whole worlds can be built inside a box. They challenge you to construct a diorama—a miniature scene contained within a shoebox, shadow box, or similar frame. The scene can be a room, a landscape, a fantasy location, a moment from a story, or a place from your imagination. The Cartographers will judge whether your tiny world feels lived in.
requirements: Create a diorama within a box or frame (shoebox, shadow box, etc.)
Build the environment using mixed media (clay, cardboard, foam, found objects)
Show clear scale and proportion in the miniature elements
Include a narrative element (a moment, a story, a character)
Document the planning and construction process

levels.4: Masterful miniature construction; materials are used intentionally and skillfully.
levels.3: Good construction with minor craftsmanship issues.
levels.2: Basic construction; some elements look unfinished.
levels.1: Poor construction; diorama is unstable or incomplete.

levels.4: Excellent spatial composition; scale is consistent and convincing.
levels.3: Good composition with minor scale issues.
levels.2: Uneven composition; scale is inconsistent.
levels.1: Poor composition; scale is unclear.

levels.4: The miniature world tells a compelling story; atmosphere is rich and believable.
levels.3: Clear narrative with good atmosphere.
levels.2: Partial narrative; atmosphere is weak.
levels.1: No clear narrative or atmosphere.
